findings.title: Preserve the light-theme color of embedded-post metadata links
findings.body: This conversion changes the light-theme lightness from 30% to 70%, rather than preserving it. In a black/white light scheme, the small embedded-post metadata link changes from #4d4d4d to #b3b3b3, giving only about 2:1 contrast against the light background and making the navigation link difficult to read. Retain 30% for $primary in the light branch and use the complementary 70% for $secondary in the dark branch.

findings.title: Keep notification badge text readable on the new dark background
findings.body: The dark-theme background now uses a dark shade derived from $secondary, but both the badge foreground and its [href] foreground still use $secondary. With a black secondary color, this produces black 11px text on #4d4d4d, approximately 2.5:1 contrast, replacing the previously light background. Generic notification badges without a subclass background override become difficult to read. Adjust the dark-theme foreground, including the [href] rule, or choose a background with sufficient contrast.

findings.title: Preserve the stronger light-theme contrast of topic-map headings
findings.body: The light branch changes the topic-map heading lightness from 20% to 50%. These headings are only 1em and normal-weight; in a black/white light scheme their color changes from #333333 to #808080 on the near-white topic-map background, dropping contrast below 4.5:1. This introduces a light-theme readability regression while fixing dark themes. Preserve 20% for the light branch and use 80% for the dark branch, as the desktop heading rule does.

findings.title: Preserve the original light-theme contrast of group-member names
findings.body: The group-member name's light-theme lightness changes from 30% to 50%. On the white user-stream item background, a black primary color now produces #808080 instead of #4d4d4d, reducing normal-sized text contrast from about 8.5:1 to 4:1. The same regression occurs in mobile/user.scss at line 497. Preserve the original 30% light branch and use the complementary 70% dark branch in both files.
